question: Tokyo Olympian C. A. Bhavani Devi is associated with which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fencing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chadalavada Anandha Sundhararaman Bhavani Devi, popularly known as C. A. Bhavani Devi, is an Indian fencer from Chennai, Tamil Nadu.

• She became the first Indian fencer to qualify for the Olympic Games, competing at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics (held in 2021) in the Sabre event.

• Fencing is a combat sport of sword-fighting (तलवारबाज़ी) contested in three weapon categories — Foil, Épée and Sabre.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bhavani Devi won a Gold medal in the sabre event at the Commonwealth Fencing Championship 2018 at Canberra, Australia.

• She is coached by Nicola Zanotti and has been supported under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS).

• India's fencing is governed by the Fencing Association of India (FAI).

NOTE

• Shooting (Option 2): A precision sport associated with Indian Olympic medallists like Abhinav Bindra and Manu Bhaker, not Bhavani Devi.

• Badminton (Option 3): A racket sport whose famous Indian players include P. V. Sindhu and Saina Nehwal.

• Gymnastics (Option 4): Associated with Indian gymnast Dipa Karmakar, the first Indian woman gymnast to qualify for the Olympics.

question: As of 31st May 2025, who is the Chairman of the Bar Council of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manan Kumar Mishra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of 31st May 2025, Manan Kumar Mishra is the Chairman of the Bar Council of India (BCI).

• The Bar Council of India (भारतीय विधिज्ञ परिषद) is a statutory body established under the Advocates Act, 1961.

• It regulates legal practice and legal education in India and lays down standards of professional conduct for advocates.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The BCI is headquartered in New Delhi.

• It prescribes the All India Bar Examination (AIBE), which advocates must clear to practise law.

• Manan Kumar Mishra, a senior advocate, has served multiple terms as BCI Chairman and is also a Rajya Sabha MP.

NOTE

• Ashok Arora (Option 1): A senior advocate and former Secretary of the Supreme Court Bar Association, not the BCI Chairman.

• Vikas Singh (Option 3): A senior advocate who served as President of the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) — a different body from the BCI.

• Dushyant Dave (Option 4): A senior advocate and former President of the Supreme Court Bar Association, not the BCI Chairman.

question: In 2025, the Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP), launched EmpowHER Biz – Sapno Ki Udaan in partnership with ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Shop.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2025, the Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP) of NITI Aayog launched EmpowHER Biz – Sapno Ki Udaan in partnership with New Shop, India's largest convenience retail chain.

• The initiative aims to empower women entrepreneurs in the retail sector (महिला उद्यमिता) by providing mentorship, market access and financial support.

• It seeks to help women set up and scale retail businesses / convenience stores across India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP) was launched by NITI Aayog in 2018.

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.

• The current CEO of NITI Aayog (2025) is B. V. R. Subrahmanyam; its Chairperson is the Prime Minister of India.

NOTE

• TATA Trusts (Option 2): A philanthropic organisation of the Tata Group; not the partner for this WEP initiative.

• Azad Foundation (Option 3): An NGO known for training women in non-traditional livelihoods such as professional driving, but not associated with EmpowHER Biz.

• JIO World (Option 4): Refers to Reliance's Jio World Centre/Convention Centre in Mumbai, unrelated to this scheme.

question: Announced in the Union Budget 2025–26, what is the primary objective of the National Geospatial Mission?
option_1: To create and manage an integrated geospatial infrastructure for governance and development
option_2: To promote satellite launch services for private companies
option_3: To provide free GPS services to rural areas
option_4: To monitor climate change patterns through satellite data
solution_text:
The correct answer is To create and manage an integrated geospatial infrastructure for governance and development.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Geospatial Mission was announced in the Union Budget 2025–26 by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.

• Its primary objective is to develop foundational geospatial infrastructure and data (भू-स्थानिक अवसंरचना) for governance and development.

• It supports the modernisation of land records, urban planning and infrastructure projects using accurate geospatial data.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The mission builds on the National Geospatial Policy, 2022, which liberalised the geospatial sector.

• It leverages the PM Gati Shakti platform for integrated infrastructure planning.

• The Union Budget 2025–26 was presented on 1 February 2025.

NOTE

• To promote satellite launch services for private companies (Option 2): This relates to space-sector reforms via IN-SPACe and NSIL, not the Geospatial Mission.

• To provide free GPS services to rural areas (Option 3): A distractor; GPS is a US navigation system, while India's own system is NavIC (IRNSS).

• To monitor climate change patterns through satellite data (Option 4): This is an objective of Earth-observation programmes, not the National Geospatial Mission.

question: Which index in 2025 highlighted that account ownership in India has reached to 89% since 2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Global Findex 2025.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Global Findex 2025, released by the World Bank, highlighted that account ownership in India rose sharply to about 89% of adults, up from around 35% in 2011.

• The Global Findex Database (वैश्विक फिनडेक्स) measures how adults save, borrow, make payments and manage financial risk worldwide.

• India's gains are credited largely to the PM Jan Dhan Yojana and the JAM trinity (Jan Dhan–Aadhaar–Mobile).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Global Findex is published by the World Bank roughly every three years (2011, 2014, 2017, 2021, 2025).

• The report also flagged high account inactivity in India despite high ownership.

• The World Bank is headquartered in Washington, D.C.; its President (2025) is Ajay Banga.

NOTE

• Fiscal Health Index 2025 (Option 2): Released by NITI Aayog, it ranks Indian states on fiscal health, not account ownership.

• Gross Financial Index 2025 (Option 3): Not an established index; a distractor term.

• National Strategy for Financial Education (Option 4): An RBI/NCFE policy framework (2020–2025) for financial literacy, not an index measuring account ownership.

question: Project ______ is the world's first inter-continental large wild carnivore translocation project.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cheetah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Project Cheetah is the world's first inter-continental large wild carnivore translocation project (चीता).

• Under it, cheetahs were brought from Africa (Namibia and South Africa) to India and released in Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh.

• The first batch of 8 cheetahs from Namibia was released by PM Narendra Modi on 17 September 2022.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The cheetah had become extinct in India in 1952; the last ones died in present-day Chhattisgarh.

• Kuno National Park is located in the Sheopur district of Madhya Pradesh.

• The cheetah is the fastest land animal, capable of speeds over 100 km/h.

NOTE

• Lion (Option 1): The Asiatic lion survives only in Gir National Park, Gujarat; conservation efforts here are the Asiatic Lion Reintroduction Project, not inter-continental.

• Crocodile (Option 3): India runs the Crocodile Conservation Project (1975) for gharials, muggers and saltwater crocodiles — a domestic breeding programme.

• Panther (Option 4): A melanistic form of leopard/jaguar; not the subject of any inter-continental translocation project.

question: Who is the author of the book 'The Illicit Happiness of Other People'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manu Joseph.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'The Illicit Happiness of Other People' (2012) is a novel written by the Indian author and journalist Manu Joseph.

• The novel is set in Madras (Chennai) and explores the mystery surrounding the death of a teenage boy through his family.

• Manu Joseph is known for his sharp, satirical writing style (व्यंग्यात्मक लेखन).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Manu Joseph's debut novel 'Serious Men' (2010) won The Hindu Literary Prize and the PEN/Open Book Award.

• 'Serious Men' was later adapted into a Netflix film directed by Sudhir Mishra.

• Manu Joseph is also a former editor of Open magazine and a noted columnist.

NOTE

• Janice Pariat (Option 1): A writer from Shillong; author of 'Boats on Land' and 'Everything the Light Touches'.

• Madhuri Vijay (Option 2): Author of 'The Far Field', which won the JCB Prize for Literature (2019).

• Neel Mukherjee (Option 3): Author of 'The Lives of Others', shortlisted for the Man Booker Prize (2014).

question: 'Abhanga Vanis' are folk songs of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Abhanga' (अभंग वाणी) is a form of devotional poetry / folk song sung in Marathi, belonging to Maharashtra.

• Abhangas are associated with the Warkari / Bhakti tradition and are sung in praise of Lord Vithoba (Vitthal) of Pandharpur.

• Famous composers of abhangas include saints Tukaram, Dnyaneshwar, Namdev and Eknath.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The word 'Abhang' literally means 'unbroken' or 'without break', denoting a continuous, imperishable devotional composition.

• The Warkari sect undertakes an annual pilgrimage (Wari) to Pandharpur singing abhangs.

• Lavani and Powada are other well-known folk-music/dance forms of Maharashtra.

NOTE

• Manipur (Option 1): Known for the classical Manipuri dance and folk forms like Lai Haraoba, not abhangas.

• West Bengal (Option 2): Famous for Baul songs and Rabindra Sangeet.

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Known for devotional Thevaram and Tiruppugazh hymns, not Marathi abhangas.

question: The 'Jhoda' dance, performed on a full moon night around Holi, belongs to which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttarakhand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jhoda is a popular folk dance of the Kumaon region of Uttarakhand (उत्तराखंड).

• It is a community dance in which men and women hold hands, form a large circle and dance while singing, often on festive full-moon nights around Holi.

• The word 'Jhoda' refers to the collective, chain-like circular formation of dancers.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other famous folk dances of Uttarakhand include Chholiya, Langvir, Barada Nati and Jhumaila.

• Chholiya is a sword dance performed mainly at weddings in the Kumaon region.

• Uttarakhand was carved out of Uttar Pradesh and became a separate state on 9 November 2000.

NOTE

• Goa (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Dekhni, Fugdi and Dhalo.

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Associated with the classical dance Kuchipudi.

• Karnataka (Option 4): Known for Yakshagana and the classical form Bharatanatyam-linked traditions; Jhoda is not from here.

question: If a satellite is in the plane of the equator with 0 degrees inclination and at a height of about 36000 km then it is said to be in ______ orbit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Geo-stationary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A satellite orbiting in the plane of the equator (0° inclination) at a height of about 36,000 km with an orbital period of 24 hours is in a geo-stationary orbit (भू-स्थिर कक्षा).

• Such a satellite appears stationary relative to a point on the Earth's surface because it moves in the same direction and period as Earth's rotation.

• Geo-stationary satellites are ideal for communication, television broadcasting and weather monitoring.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The concept of the geostationary orbit was popularised by science-fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke, so it is also called the Clarke Orbit.

• India's INSAT and GSAT series satellites are placed in geostationary orbit.

• A geosynchronous orbit has a 24-hour period but may be inclined; a geostationary orbit is a special geosynchronous orbit with 0° inclination.

NOTE

• Polar (Option 1): A low-altitude orbit passing over the poles (near 90° inclination), used for Earth observation and remote sensing.

• Elliptical (Option 3): An oval-shaped orbit with varying distance from Earth, not the equatorial 36,000 km circular orbit described.

• Sun-synchronous (Option 4): A special near-polar orbit that passes over a location at the same local solar time, used by remote-sensing satellites.

question: Which of the following is NOT a main factor affecting the rate of evaporation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Buoyancy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Buoyancy (उत्प्लावकता) is the upward force exerted by a fluid on an immersed object and is NOT a factor affecting the rate of evaporation.

• The rate of evaporation mainly depends on surface area, temperature, wind speed and humidity.

• Larger surface area, higher temperature and greater wind speed increase evaporation, while higher humidity decreases it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Evaporation is a surface phenomenon in which a liquid changes to vapour below its boiling point.

• Evaporation causes cooling because the fastest (most energetic) molecules escape, lowering the average energy of the remaining liquid.

• Buoyancy is explained by Archimedes' Principle.

NOTE

• Surface area (Option 1): A genuine factor — a larger exposed surface increases the rate of evaporation.

• Wind speed (Option 3): A genuine factor — higher wind speed carries away vapour molecules, increasing evaporation.

• Humidity (Option 4): A genuine factor — higher humidity slows evaporation as the air is already saturated with water vapour.

question: What is gravitational potential energy?
option_1: Energy possessed by an object due to its motion
option_2: Energy stored in an object due to its position above the ground
option_3: Energy that is released during a chemical reaction
solution_text:
The correct answer is Energy stored in an object due to its position above the ground.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gravitational potential energy (गुरुत्वीय स्थितिज ऊर्जा) is the energy stored in an object because of its position/height above the ground.

• It is given by the formula PE = mgh, where m = mass, g = acceleration due to gravity, and h = height.

• The higher an object is raised, the greater its gravitational potential energy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The SI unit of energy is the Joule (J).

• When an object falls, its gravitational potential energy converts into kinetic energy, illustrating the law of conservation of energy.

• The value of g on Earth's surface is about 9.8 m/s².

NOTE

• Energy possessed by an object due to its motion (Option 1): This defines kinetic energy (KE = ½mv²), not potential energy.

• Energy that is released during a chemical reaction (Option 3): This refers to chemical energy.

• Energy transferred through heat (Option 4): This describes thermal/heat energy, not gravitational potential energy.

question: India's first airport based self-powered indoor air quality monitoring facility 'Pavana Chitra' was unveiled at which airport in October 2024?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thiruvananthapuram International Airport.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's first airport-based self-powered indoor air quality monitoring facility 'Pavana Chitra' (पवन चित्र) was unveiled at Thiruvananthapuram International Airport in October 2024.

• It was dedicated by Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh.

• The facility is self-powered (energy self-sufficient) and monitors indoor air quality for passengers and staff.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The technology was developed by CSIR–National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology (NIIST), Thiruvananthapuram.

• Thiruvananthapuram International Airport is located in Kerala and is one of India's oldest airports.

• CSIR (Council of Scientific and Industrial Research) was established in 1942.

NOTE

• Chennai International Airport (Option 1): A major airport in Tamil Nadu, but not the site of the Pavana Chitra launch.

• Bengaluru International Airport (Option 2): The Kempegowda International Airport in Karnataka; not associated with this facility.

• Jaipur International Airport (Option 3): An airport in Rajasthan, unrelated to the Pavana Chitra project.

question: Which railway zone became India's first to switch to compostable bioplastic on trains in August 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Northeast Frontier Railway.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In August 2025, the Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR) (पूर्वोत्तर सीमा रेलवे) became India's first railway zone to switch to compostable bioplastic on trains.

• NFR introduced biodegradable/compostable bedroll and bag materials, developed in collaboration with IIT Guwahati.

• The move aims to replace single-use plastics and reduce environmental pollution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Northeast Frontier Railway is headquartered at Maligaon, Guwahati (Assam).

• Indian Railways currently has 19 railway zones.

• Indian Railways is pursuing a target of becoming a 'Net Zero Carbon Emitter'.

NOTE

• Northern Railway (Option 1): Headquartered at Baroda House, New Delhi; not the first to adopt compostable bioplastic.

• Southern Railway (Option 2): Headquartered at Chennai; India's first railway zone by formation (1951), but unrelated to this initiative.

• Western Railway (Option 3): Headquartered at Churchgate, Mumbai; not associated with this milestone.

question:
Which of the following Mughal Emperor was assassinated by his nobles?
I. Farrukh Siyar
II. Alamgir II
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both Mughal emperors Farrukh Siyar and Alamgir II were assassinated by their own nobles (सरदारों द्वारा हत्या).

• Farrukh Siyar (r. 1713–1719) was blinded, deposed and killed by the powerful Sayyid Brothers (Abdullah Khan and Hussain Ali Khan).

• Alamgir II (r. 1754–1759) was murdered on the orders of his own wazir Imad-ul-Mulk (Ghazi-ud-Din Khan).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Sayyid Brothers were known as the 'King Makers' of the later Mughal period.

• Farrukh Siyar granted the East India Company's 1717 farman, allowing duty-free trade in Bengal.

• The rapid rise and fall of later Mughal rulers reflected the decline of the Mughal Empire after Aurangzeb's death in 1707.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete — Farrukh Siyar was assassinated, but so was Alamgir II.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete — Alamgir II was assassinated, but so was Farrukh Siyar.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect — both emperors were indeed murdered by nobles.

question: In the context of Microeconomics, the graphical representation of the demand function is called the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is demand curve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In microeconomics, the graphical representation of the demand function is called the demand curve (मांग वक्र).

• It shows the relationship between the price of a good and the quantity demanded, other factors remaining constant.

• The demand curve normally slopes downward from left to right, reflecting the Law of Demand (price and quantity demanded are inversely related).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The demand curve is drawn with price on the Y-axis and quantity demanded on the X-axis.

• A movement along the curve is a change in quantity demanded, while a shift of the entire curve is a change in demand.

• Goods that violate the law of demand include Giffen goods and Veblen goods.

NOTE

• goods curve (Option 2): Not a standard economic term; a distractor.

• supply curve (Option 3): Represents the supply function, showing the relation between price and quantity supplied (upward sloping).

• seller curve (Option 4): Not a recognised economic concept; a distractor.

question: The National Infrastructure Pipeline was launched in India in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2020.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) (राष्ट्रीय अवसंरचना पाइपलाइन) was launched in India in 2020 (announced end of 2019, formally rolled out in 2020).

• It is a first-of-its-kind initiative to provide world-class infrastructure across the country and improve the quality of life of citizens.

• It aimed for an initial investment of about ₹111 lakh crore over the period 2020–2025.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The NIP covers sectors such as energy, roads, railways, urban infrastructure and irrigation.

• It was formulated by a task force headed by then Economic Affairs Secretary Atanu Chakraborty.

• The NIP is closely linked with the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan launched in 2021.

NOTE

• 2003 (Option 1): Year associated with the FRBM Act enactment (passed 2003), not the NIP.

• 2008 (Option 2): Year of the global financial crisis; unrelated to the NIP.

• 2013 (Option 3): Incorrect; the NIP did not exist then.

question: Abhijit Sen was the chairman of the Committee on the Wholesale Price Index which submitted its report in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2008.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Economist Abhijit Sen chaired the Working Group / Committee on the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) (थोक कीमत सूचकांक), which submitted its report in 2008.

• The committee recommended revising the base year of the WPI and updating the basket of commodities.

• Based on its recommendations, the WPI base year was later revised to 2004–05.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Abhijit Sen was an agricultural economist and a former member of the Planning Commission of India.

• The WPI in India is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

• The current WPI base year is 2011–12.

NOTE

• 2004 (Option 1): Incorrect year; the report was submitted in 2008.

• 2010 (Option 3): Incorrect; a distractor year.

• 2006 (Option 4): Incorrect; the committee submitted its report in 2008.

question: Which of the following subjects falls under the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Criminal matters.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Criminal matters — including criminal law and criminal procedure (दंड के मामले) — fall under the Concurrent List of the Indian Constitution.

• Both the Union (Centre) and the State governments can legislate on subjects in the Concurrent List.

• The Concurrent List is contained in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Seventh Schedule has three lists — Union List, State List and Concurrent List.

• If a central and a state law on a concurrent subject conflict, the central law prevails (Article 254).

• Other Concurrent List subjects include education, marriage and divorce, forests, and bankruptcy.

NOTE

• Police (Option 1): A State List subject (public order and police are state responsibilities).

• Radio and television (Option 3): A Union List subject (posts, telegraphs, telephones, broadcasting).

• Foreign affairs (Option 4): A Union List subject handled exclusively by the central government.

question: Which of the following is NOT a cropping season in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barani.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Barani (बारानी) is NOT a cropping season in India; it refers to rain-fed agriculture (farming that depends on rainfall rather than irrigation).

• India has three main cropping seasons — Kharif, Rabi and Zaid.

• The three genuine seasons are based on the monsoon and climatic cycle of the country.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kharif crops are sown with the onset of the southwest monsoon (June–July) and harvested in September–October; examples: rice, maize, cotton, bajra.

• Rabi crops are sown in winter (October–December) and harvested in spring (March–April); examples: wheat, gram, mustard, barley.

• Zaid crops are grown in the short summer season between Rabi and Kharif; examples: watermelon, cucumber, muskmelon.

NOTE

• Kharif (Option 1): A genuine monsoon (autumn) cropping season.

• Rabi (Option 2): A genuine winter cropping season.

• Zaid (Option 3): A genuine short summer cropping season.

question: Who among the following was the deputy chairman of Planning Commission under the tenth five year plan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is K.C. Pant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• K. C. Pant was the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission (योजना आयोग के उपाध्यक्ष) during the launch of the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002–2007).

• He served as Deputy Chairman from 1999 to 2004.

• The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairman of the Planning Commission, so the working head is the Deputy Chairman.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Tenth Five Year Plan (2002–2007) targeted a growth rate of about 8% and aimed to reduce poverty.

• The Planning Commission was established in 1950 and replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015.

• After K. C. Pant, Montek Singh Ahluwalia became Deputy Chairman (2004–2014).

NOTE

• Shankarrao Chavan (Option 1): A senior Congress leader who served as Union Home Minister and Finance Minister and Chief Minister of Maharashtra, not this post.

• Yaswant Sinha (Option 3): Served as Union Finance Minister and External Affairs Minister, not Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

• P. Shiv Shankar (Option 4): A Congress leader who held ministries such as Law and External Affairs, not this post.

question:
In the context of trade policy tools, Which of the following is considered as non-tariff measure?
I. Anti-dumping measures
II. Technical barriers to trade measures
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both anti-dumping measures and technical barriers to trade (TBT) are considered non-tariff measures (गैर-प्रशुल्क उपाय) in trade policy.

• Non-tariff measures are trade barriers other than customs duties/tariffs that restrict or regulate imports and exports.

• Anti-dumping duties protect domestic industry from goods sold below fair value, while TBTs relate to standards, testing and certification requirements.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Non-tariff measures also include quotas, licences, subsidies and sanitary/phyto-sanitary (SPS) measures.

• These are regulated under the World Trade Organization (WTO), established in 1995, headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

• A tariff, by contrast, is a tax/duty imposed on imports or exports.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete — technical barriers to trade are also non-tariff measures.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete — anti-dumping measures are also non-tariff measures.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect — both are recognised non-tariff measures.

question: What led to the decline in mortality rate in India during 1921-1951?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Improved health and sanitation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The decline in India's mortality (death) rate during 1921–1951 was mainly due to improved health and sanitation (बेहतर स्वास्थ्य और स्वच्छता) facilities.

• Better control of epidemics, famines and diseases, along with advances in medicine and public health, reduced deaths.

• The year 1921 is regarded as the 'Great Divide' or 'Demographic Divide' in India's population history, after which the death rate fell steadily.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• After 1921, India's population grew steadily due to a falling death rate while the birth rate remained high.

• The period 1921–1951 marks the second phase (steady growth) of India's demographic history.

• Census in India is conducted every 10 years; the first complete census was in 1881.

NOTE

• Second world war (Option 1): The war (1939–1945) generally caused hardship and the Bengal Famine of 1943; it did not lower the mortality rate.

• Increase in birth rate (Option 3): A higher birth rate affects population growth, not the death (mortality) rate.

• Artificial intelligence (Option 4): An anachronistic distractor — AI did not exist during 1921–1951.

question: What are the temporary finger-like extensions of the cell surface used by Amoeba to take in food called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pseudopodia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The temporary finger-like extensions of the cell surface used by Amoeba to take in food are called pseudopodia (स्यूडोपोडिया / पादाभ), meaning 'false feet'.

• Amoeba engulfs food using these pseudopodia through a process called phagocytosis (endocytosis).

• Pseudopodia are also used by Amoeba for movement (locomotion).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The mode of nutrition in Amoeba is holozoic (ingesting solid food particles).

• The engulfed food is digested inside a food vacuole.

• Amoeba is a unicellular organism belonging to the Kingdom Protista.

NOTE

• Flagella (Option 1): Long whip-like structures used for movement, e.g., in Euglena and sperm cells.

• Cilia (Option 2): Short hair-like structures used for movement and feeding, e.g., in Paramecium.

• Vacuoles (Option 3): Membrane-bound sacs inside the cell for storage and digestion (e.g., food and contractile vacuoles), not for capturing food from outside.

question: What does 'moksha' stand for in the fourfold objective of life according to Vedic philosophy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Spiritual freedom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the fourfold objective of life (Purusharthas) of Vedic philosophy, 'Moksha' stands for spiritual freedom / liberation (आध्यात्मिक स्वतंत्रता).

• Moksha means liberation of the soul from the cycle of birth and death (samsara) and union with the ultimate reality.

• It is regarded as the highest and final goal among the four Purusharthas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The four Purusharthas are Dharma (righteousness/duty), Artha (wealth), Kama (desire) and Moksha (liberation).

• Dharma is considered the foundation that regulates the pursuit of Artha and Kama.

• The concept of Moksha is central to Hindu, Jain and Buddhist (Nirvana) thought.

NOTE

• Pursuit of desires (Option 1): This corresponds to Kama (desire/pleasure), not Moksha.

• Social status (Option 2): Not one of the Purusharthas; a distractor.

• Wealth accumulation (Option 4): This corresponds to Artha (material wealth), not Moksha.
